alternate_names: Shri Baba Dhopeshwar Nath Ji Temple
deities: Parvati (worshipped in one form with Shiva in the lingam)

history.period: Legendary - Dwapar Yuga / Mahabharata era per tradition (unverifiable); ~5000 years claimed
history.summary: A water temple (talab/kund) in the Bareilly Cantonment area, counted among the seven Nath temples of Nath Nagari. Legend says Dhrum Rishi, guru of Draupadi, did penance here in the Dwapar Yuga and established the swayambhu shivling in which Shiva and Parvati are worshipped in one form; devotees reach the sanctum wading through a tunnel. Bathing in the temple lake is believed to cure allergies; the concrete steps on its banks are traditionally credited to an order from the Begum of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh after a fulfilled vow. name: Baba Dhopeshwar Nath Temple
town_description: Bareilly is a major city in western Uttar Pradesh on the northern Gangetic plain, traditionally called Nath Nagari for its cluster of ancient Shiva temples. A historic trade and cantonment town, it is known for zardozi embroidery, furniture and the Ala Hazrat dargah alongside its Hindu shrines, and is well connected by rail and road to Delhi and Lucknow.

travel.road: End of Dhopa Road, Bareilly Cantonment; local buses, taxis and autos available.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February; large crowds at Shivaratri, Janmashtami and Sawan Mondays.
